Understanding INS Numbers

Learn about the International Numbering System used globally to classify food additives.

What is the INS?

The International Numbering System for Food Additives (INS) is a codex classification system that provides a standardized, language-independent way to identify additives.

Designed by the Codex Alimentarius Commission, it helps consumers and regulatory bodies identify ingredients across borders without relying on complex chemical names.

Why are INS Numbers Used?

🌐

Global Standardization

Ensures food packages in any country use the same identification codes, easing trade and safety tracking.

🔍

Consumer Awareness

Allows consumers to track and avoid specific compounds linked to allergies or diet choices.

⚕️

Regulatory Tracking

Helps food safety agencies update approvals, limits, and warning mandates for specific codes easily.
